subject.title: fix(irc): disconnect on oversized inbound lines

question: After an oversized inbound IRC record closes the socket, should the account automatically reconnect with bounded backoff, or intentionally remain offline until operator recovery?
rationale: Both behaviors are plausible operational policies, but the client-only patch and proof do not establish which lifecycle the IRC channel promises after a protocol violation.

options.title: Prove bounded recovery
options.body: Add account-level coverage showing that the monitor reconnects safely with bounded backoff and cannot enter a tight hostile-server loop.

options.title: Accept terminal disconnect
options.body: Land the fail-closed behavior only after confirming that remaining offline is intentional and that status or logs provide a clear operator recovery path.

options.title: Pause pending IRC policy
options.body: Hold the PR until the IRC owner chooses the permanent post-violation lifecycle contract.

recommendation.title: Prove bounded recovery
recommendation.body: Add account-level coverage showing that the monitor reconnects safely with bounded backoff and cannot enter a tight hostile-server loop.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository explicitly assigns IRC ownership to this account, making it the best available owner for the disconnect and recovery policy.
